ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$7.06 (5.01 km × S$1.4098/km) to the rider as a voucher per NS-7, and record the driver's unexcused 5.01 km deviation as a breach of the shortest-and-most-direct-route obligation for Ryde's monitoring.
ruling.reasoning:
Service type is RydeTAXI (metered), so the formula is RD-2 metered branch: unexempt segment extra_km × this trip's per-km rate (F4: distance fare ÷ distance km = $1.4098/km). Only the mileage unit is refunded; stop/wait time is dealt with separately.

Route deviation: F3 records one off-route segment 09:13–09:24, 6.58 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.57 km, adding 5.01 km [F3] (consistent with the trip-level +5.4 km at +50% [F1]). The deviation is unexplained unless an exemption applies.

Exemptions examined: RD-5 fails for lack of consent — F7 shows no in-app chat at all, so no pre-departure agreement exists; the driver's post-trip written claim that it was reasonable [F8] is a statement, not rider consent (G11). RD-3 fails: no rider-named stop or destination change appears anywhere in the record. RD-4 fails: the driver invokes congestion/flooding ("Ayer Rajah Expressway was crawling") [F8], but the only supporting traffic facts are speed bands on AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY (band 2, 10–19 km/h) [F9], CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY (band 5) [F10] and KENT RIDGE ROAD (band 3) [F11], and no traffic incident is recorded near the route [F12]. Under RD-4(a) an exemption needs a DataMall incident on the replaced optimal-route segment (m_from_route ≤ 300 m, reported before the segment start); there is none [F12]. Under RD-4(b) a speed band alone — even band 2 [F9], whose window 08:49–09:13 only partly overlaps the 09:13–09:24 detour — is corroborative at most and cannot exempt by itself in the MVP pending Ryde's confirmation (G3). Heavy rain [F13] is not a per-se clause ground either. The segment is therefore unexempted and counts as a deviation under RD-1/RD-2.

Amount: 5.01 km [F3] × $1.4098/km [F4] = $7.0631 → $7.06. The fare's other excess-distance arithmetic uses 5.34 km ($7.53) [F4]; per RD-2 only extra_km of the unexempt segment is refundable, and the residual corridor/matching jitter is not. RD-6 account flag not applied: the driver's 90-day upheld route disputes are 0 [F15], so he is not a "repeated" route offender (this case may still be recorded internally).

Safety screen: read F7/F8 and the complaint; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — nothing triggering SAFE-1/SAFE-2. Evidence status sufficient (GPS, timeline, fare and traffic all present; the conflicting party statement is resolved by the system records and the absence of records tying the detour to any exemption).

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 09:13–09:24 adds 5.01 km [F3]. No rider consent exists: there are no chat messages at all [F7], and the driver's post-hoc written claim of congestion/flooding [F8] is a statement, not pre-departure consent (RD-5, G11); no rider-named stop applies (RD-3). The claimed reasonable cause fails under RD-4: no traffic incident is recorded on the replaced optimal route [F12], and the Ayer Rajah Expressway band-2 record [F9] (window 08:49–09:13, only partly covering the segment) is corroborative only and cannot exempt alone (RD-4(b), G3). The segment is unexempted and refundable under RD-2 at 5.01 km × $1.4098/km = $7.06.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip claim that AYE congestion/flooding justified the detour is unsupported as a clause-level exemption: no DataMall incident on the replaced optimal route [F12], and a speed band alone (band 2 [F9], window 08:49–09:13) is corroborative only under RD-4(b)/G3; a driver's statement is not rider consent either (RD-5, G11).
Not applied: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F15], so this case does not make him a 'repeated' route offender (RD-6).
